outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The agent includes the label “Type mnemonic: MX” and “Status mnemonic: NOERROR” even though the MX /resolve JSON view (DOM state 18) only explicitly shows numeric codes (status 0, type 15); these mnemonics are standard interpretations, so this is mostly a labeling nitpick rather than harmful. (2) The agent calls the “Result configuration heading” a “JSON summary” rather than the exact on-page “Result for example.com/MX ...” heading; since the MX evidence available is the /resolve JSON, this is a minor presentation mismatch.

Critical issues: The task explicitly asks to “Report the complete result-configuration heading” from the MX results page. In the provided DOM evidence, there is no captured MX ‘Result for example.com/MX ...’ heading—only A and erroneous AMX headings are shown (states 2/3/9 for A, 11/17 for AMX). The agent therefore did not (and could not, from the evidenced view) provide the actual MX results-page heading as requested; instead it outputs a constructed JSON block as the ‘heading’. Given the task’s specificity about the heading, this is a missing required deliverable.

On the other hand, for the MX response content itself, the agent successfully obtained an MX response from dns.google (DOM state 18 at https://dns.google/resolve?name=example.com&type=MX), and its reported numeric Status (0), flags (TC false, RD true, RA true, AD true, CD false), Question (example.com., type 15), and the single MX Answer record (name example.com., type 15, data “0 .”) match what is shown in DOM state 18. It also correctly omitted TTL in its answer list and did not introduce any RRSIG records.

Overall, despite correctly extracting almost all required MX fields, the lack of the complete MX result-configuration heading as it appears on the MX results page is a key missing element from the user’s requested report, so the task is not fully successfully completed.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted a DNS MX lookup for example.com performed using Google Public DNS’s web interface, then to extract and report specific fields from the MX result: the result heading/config summary, status (number+mnemonic), five flags (TC/RD/RA/AD/CD), question (name + type number+mnemonic), and all MX (type 15) answers (name + type number+mnemonic + data), excluding TTL and not misclassifying any RRSIG records. A reasonable user would be flexible about whether the final MX response was viewed on the “pretty” results page vs. the JSON /resolve view, as long as it is clearly from dns.google and the reported fields are correct and complete.
